NovaBiotech Therapeutics - Q3 2024 Earnings Call Transcript

Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the NovaBiotech Therapeutics Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Sarah Jenkins, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Jenkins, Head of Investor Relations:
Thank you, Operator. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss NovaBiotech Therapeutics' financial results for the third quarter of 2024. Joining me on today's call are Johnathan Hale, Chief Executive Officer; Michael Rivera, Chief Financial Officer; Dr. Emily Chen, Chief Medical Officer; and Dr. Raj Patel, Chief Scientific Officer; Lisa Moreno, Head of Commercial.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that today's call will contain forward-looking statements. These statements are based on management's current expectations and are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete discussion of these risks.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Johnathan Hale, CEO of NovaBiotech Therapeutics.

Johnathan Hale, CEO:
Thank you, Sarah. Good morning, everyone. NovaBiotech Therapeutics delivered a strong performance in the third quarter, driven by robust growth in our oncology franchise, accelerated uptake of key products like NovaVaxim and NovaLink-147, and significant momentum across our diversified pipeline. We continue to make significant progress on our key strategic priorities, including advancing late-stage clinical programs, expanding our commercial footprint globally, enhancing manufacturing efficiencies, pursuing value-creating business development deals, managing our patent exposures proactively, and positioning for sustained long-term growth.

We're particularly excited about NVB-301, our next-generation bispecific T-cell engager, and its potential to capture substantial share in the HER2-positive solid tumor market with projected peak sales exceeding $1.2 billion.

Now, I will turn the call over to Michael Rivera, our CFO, to provide a more detailed review of our financial results.

Michael Rivera, CFO:
Thank you, Johnathan. As Johnathan mentioned, we had a solid third quarter. Revenue for the quarter was $2.8 billion, an increase of 18% compared to the same period last year. This increase was primarily driven by 25% top-line expansion in our flagship oncology franchise, led by NovaVaxim, our PD-1/PD-L1 inhibitor that's now capturing 12% U.S. market share in non-small cell lung cancer, alongside strong contributions from biosimilars and rare disease assets.

Our GAAP net income for the quarter was $500 million, or $1.50 per share. Non-GAAP net income was $700 million, or $2.10 per share.

Our operating expenses were $1.6 billion, reflecting continued investments in R&D to support our pipeline, partially offset by efficiency gains in SG&A. We continue to invest heavily in R&D, up 22% year-over-year to $1.1 billion this quarter, bolstered by a 15% efficiency improvement from our AI-driven target identification platform. Our cash position remains strong at $8.2 billion.

For the full year, we are updating our guidance to revenues of $11.2-11.5 billion, up 17-19% at the midpoint, and core EPS of $6.85-7.05.

Good afternoon, everyone, and thank you for joining NovaBiotech Therapeutics' Q3 2024 earnings call. I'm thrilled to kick off our discussion on overall performance with what I can confidently call a standout quarter that underscores the strength of our diversified portfolio and the momentum in our oncology and rare disease franchises. We delivered total net product revenues of $2.48 billion from our key segments earlier, but on a consolidated basis hitting $2.8 billion overall when including collaborations, representing 28% year-over-year growth and a robust 15% sequential increase from Q2. This topped our guidance midpoint by $120 million, driven primarily by accelerated uptake of our next-gen ADC, NovaLink-147, and sustained demand for our flagship PD-L1 inhibitor, NovaVance—wait, NovaVaxim—which continues to capture share in the immuno-oncology space amid anticipation of shifts in the post-Keytruda landscape.

In oncology, now accounting for 52% of total revenues at $1.29 billion, we saw 35% YoY growth. NovaVaxim generated $875 million in U.S. net sales alone, up 22% YoY, benefiting from expanded label inclusion for frontline NSCLC following our successful sNDA approval in May. NovaLink-147, our site-specific antibody-drug conjugate targeting HER2-low breast cancer—similar to Enhertu's profile but with cleaner linker chemistry—ramped to $210 million in its first full quarter post-PDUFA, exceeding our initial $150 million forecast thanks to favorable NCCN guideline inclusion and partnerships with community oncology networks.

Our rare disease and gene therapy segment delivered $680 million, a 19% YoY increase, led by ZephyrGene, our AAV-based therapy for spinal muscular atrophy, which posted $420 million globally. This reflects deeper penetration in Type 1 and Type 2 patients, with U.S. market share now at 68% versus competitors like Spinraza and Zolgensma, supported by durable expression data from the long-term extension of our Phase III AURORA trial. Biosimilars contributed $310 million, up 45% YoY, with our adalimumab high-concentration biosimilar, NovaHumira, gaining 12% U.S. TRx share since launch, capitalizing on erosion in the originator market.

Operationally, adjusted non-GAAP EPS came in at $2.14, a 32% YoY increase and $0.29 ahead of consensus, with gross margins expanding—we'll cover that in detail shortly. Operating cash flow was a healthy $1.1 billion, bolstering our cash position to $8.7 billion, giving us ample dry powder for the $5-7 billion M&A pipeline we're actively pursuing in cell and gene modalities.

Regionally, the U.S. drove 62% of revenues at $1.54 billion, up 31% YoY, fueled by strong reimbursement under the Inflation Reduction Act's Part D redesign and value-based contracting with PBMs like CVS Caremark. Europe contributed 24% or $595 million, up 22% YoY, with EMA approvals accelerating despite pricing pressures navigated via confidential discounts. Asia-Pacific, at 11% or $273 million, up 18% YoY, saw outsized growth in China through our JV with partners like Fosun, tapping the expanding IO market.

Strategically, our AI-driven platform, NovaForge, collaborating with NVIDIA's BioNeMo, screened 1.2 million novel small molecules, yielding three IND-ready candidates in fibrosis, reducing timelines by 40%. In gene editing, we dosed the first patient in our CRISPR-Cas13 Phase I for ALS, with interim data Q1 2025.

Looking ahead, we're raising FY2024 revenue guidance to $9.85-$10.05 billion and adjusted EPS to $8.40-$8.60, implying 26% top-line growth. Q4 guidance is $2.65-$2.75 billion revenues and $2.30-$2.45 EPS.

Key takeaways include robust execution with 28% revenue growth outpacing industry averages, market share gains in IO and ADCs, 15 clinical readouts in 2025 de-risking our $25 billion peak sales pipeline, financial strength supporting M&A, and positioning in AI/ML and next-gen modalities.

Thank you, Johnathan, and good afternoon, everyone. I'll now turn to our gross margin performance and the key drivers behind our manufacturing efficiency gains, which continue to be a cornerstone of our profitability story. We operate in a capital-intensive segment, with a portfolio spanning high-value monoclonal antibodies like our flagship NeoMab-7, our biosimilar NovaHumira, and mRNA platforms like NovaVax-2.

For Q3 2024, we delivered a non-GAAP gross margin of 82.3%, up 270 basis points YoY from 79.6%, and 50 bps sequentially. This is the sixth straight quarter of expansion, with trailing 12-month at 81.5%, ahead of peers around 77%. GAAP was 80.1%, with a $12 million depreciation charge from our Singapore plant.

Mix contributed 150 bps, with NeoMab-7 at 45% of revenue driving 88% margins. NovaHumira ramped to $250 million with 85% margins and 22% EU TRx share. Volumes up 22% YoY added 80 bps, pricing flat to +2% in U.S.

Manufacturing efficiency drove 200 bps, with COGS per unit down 18% to $42 per vial. Bioreactor titers up 25% to 8.2 g/L via NovaYield AI. Continuous manufacturing at 40% of API, cutting cycles to 45 days. Single-use systems eliminated 95% cleaning downtime.

U.S. ops at 84% margins, Europe 78% offset by yields, Asia 86%. Dual-sourcing 90% materials, capex $450 million focused on mRNA scale-up. Guide Q4 82.5-83.5%, FY24 81.8-82.2%, to 85% by 2026.

Thank you, Johnathan, and good afternoon, everyone. I'll now turn to our business development activities, a cornerstone of our strategy to build a robust pipeline in oncology, immunology, and cardiometabolic diseases. In Q3, we executed three transformative deals—a licensing agreement, tuck-in acquisition, and expanded partnership—adding over $2.5 billion in projected peak sales at NPV. These bolster late-stage assets ahead of 2026 patent cliffs on our legacy JAK inhibitor, positioning us in the $150 billion ADC and GLP-1 markets.

On licensing, we in-licensed global rights excluding Greater China to NX-401 from Nexus Biotech, Phase II-ready ADC for HER2-low breast cancer, mirroring Enhertu with 65% ORR preclinical. $250 million upfront, $1.2 billion milestones, 18% royalties. Peak $800 million U.S. by 2032, Phase II H2 2025. Asia sourcing cuts costs 30-40%.

Acquisitions: $850 million for GeneForge Therapeutics' CRISPR GF-Edit for cardiomyopathies, IND Q1 2026. $550 million cash, $200 million stock, $100 million contingent. Diversifies to cell/gene, UK tax credits.

Partnerships: Expanded Roche alliance on NB-GLP2, dual agonist with 22% weight loss. Adds $750 million opt-ins, 50/50 split, $1.5 billion our share. Roche's AI optimizes dosing.

Aggregate: top 10 assets $15 billion rNPV, 60% Phase II/III. String of pearls deals preserve $4.2 billion runway. 40% Asia, 30% Europe BD. Five term sheets Q4.

Now, good morning, everyone. As we wrap up a transformative Q3, I want to pivot to our strategic priorities and multi-year outlook. Our North Star: high-teens revenue growth via pipeline innovation, commercial execution, capital allocation.

First pillar: late-stage pipeline. NVB-301 78% ORR Phase 3, BLA Q1 2025. NVB-402 ADC interim mid-2025. NVB-512 Alzheimer's Phase 3 H2 2026. NVB-GT1 Pompe Phase 2.

Second: commercial excellence. NovaVaxim $1.9 billion YTD, NVB-Rheum $850 million. Biosimilars $420 million, $2 billion by 2027.

Third: global expansion. U.S. 65%, Europe 20%, China doubled to $280 million.

Fourth: agility. SG&A 22%, gross 82%, $1.2 billion GeneX acquisition.

2025: 16-20% growth to $13.2-14.0 billion, EPS $8.10-8.70. Long-term 15%+ CAGR to $22 billion.

Good afternoon, everyone. Before questions, deeper on patent cliff exposure and lifecycle strategies. Industry $250 billion cliff 2025-2030. Our Nexavolt GLP-1 $2.8 billion (42% revenue), expiry Q4 2026; LipiShield PCSK9 $1.4 billion (21%), mid-2027. Modeled 28-32% trough.

Mitigation: label expansions—Nexavolt monthly injector, pediatric, NASH PDUFA Nov 2024 (45% fat reduction). LipiShield CKD Phase IIIb Q4 2024.

Formulations: Nexavolt XR oral $900 million peak. LSP-301 bispecific Phase II.

Regional: U.S. pricing fortress, Europe 10-year exclusivity, China 35% growth.

R&D 22%, M&A like $2.2 billion Oncura. $18 billion NPV, 8-10% CAGR post-2027.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Dr. Emily Chen, our Chief Medical Officer, to discuss our clinical programs.

Dr. Emily Chen, Chief Medical Officer:
Thank you, Michael. We are very pleased with the progress of our clinical trials. Before we open for Q&A, I'd like to provide a comprehensive update on our clinical pipeline, the cornerstone of NovaBiotech's value creation. We're focused on precision oncology and immuno-oncology, with six clinical assets leveraging AetherLink tumor microenvironment platform for NSCLC, TNBC, PDAC.

Flagship ATH-301 bispecific PD-1/Claudin-18.2 for gastric/GEJ: completed 720-patient Phase 3 AETHERA-301 enrollment, topline PFS Q4 2024, OS H1 2025. Phase 2 68% ORR, 14.2-month PFS. RMAT FDA, PRIME EMA, PMDA/NMPA advice. BeiGene China partnership. 2026 launch, $4.5 billion market.

ATH-202 CAR-T HER2: Phase 2 52% ORR TNBC, 18.4-month DOR, Phase 3 Q1 2025, Fast Track. 14-day vein-to-vein.

ATH-401 PD-L1/VEGF Phase 1b/2: 44% ORR, readout Q3 2025.

ATH-501 STING ADC IND cleared, dosing Q4 2024. Orphan for PDAC.

PTS 65% late-stage. R&D $180 million, $650 million runway. 55% U.S. enrollment.

Two Phase 3 readouts, three designations, $3 billion peak. Operator ready.

Next, Dr. Raj Patel will provide an update on our research pipeline.

Dr. Raj Patel, Chief Scientific Officer:
Thank you, Dr. Chen. We are making significant strides in our early-stage research. Building on our preclinical momentum, we're advancing AI-optimized targets in fibrosis, neurodegeneration PROTACs, and RNA therapeutics post-mRNA. Our NovaYield and NovaForge platforms have identified novel payloads for next-gen ADCs, with bystander activity surpassing peers. In gene editing, GF-Edit enhancements target off-targets, supporting INDs in cardiomyopathies and ALS. Preclinical titers hit 90% expression for AAV9 in Pompe. We're prioritizing modalities like CRISPR-Cas13 and bispecifics, with five preclinical assets entering IND-enabling studies Q4, de-risked by NVIDIA simulations cutting timelines 30%. This early pipeline adds $12 billion rNPV, diversifying beyond oncology into cardio-metabolic and neuro.

Now I'll turn the call over to Lisa Moreno, Head of Commercial, to discuss product sales and marketing.

Lisa Moreno, Head of Commercial:
Thank you, Dr. Patel. Our sales performance this quarter was outstanding, with 28% YoY growth led by oncology at 35%. NovaVaxim hit $875 million U.S., label expansions driving 95% patient access. NovaLink-147 exceeded $210 million launch, NCCN inclusion key. Biosimilars like NovaHumira captured 12% U.S. share, Europe 22%. Rare diseases ZephyrGene 68% share. Marketing campaigns effective in IO via digital patient journeys and KOL engagement, boosting adherence 15%. Global push: China doubled via JVs, Medicare tailwinds U.S. Q4 seasonal stocking.

Now, I'll hand the call back to Johnathan.

Johnathan Hale, CEO:
Thank you, Lisa. We will now open the call for questions.

Operator:
Ladies and gentlemen, instructions for the question-and-answer session. Our first question comes from David Lee with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

David Lee, Goldman Sachs:
Thanks, and congrats on the quarter. On business development, can you elaborate on the NX-401 licensing and how it fits with your ADC strategy amid competition?

Michael Rivera, CFO:
Thanks, David. NX-401's profile with 65% ORR and proprietary linker slots perfectly into our infrastructure, forecasting $800 million peak U.S. It's bolt-on from Asia, low upfront $250 million, high milestones, hedging our JAK cliff while capturing ADC growth.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Rachel Kim with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Rachel Kim, JPMorgan:
Great, thanks. On gross margins, what gives you confidence in 85% by 2026 with inflation?

Michael Rivera, CFO:
Rachel, yield gains to 8.2 g/L and continuous manufacturing scaling to 70% are key, plus Singapore hub at 86%. Inflation hedged by long-term contracts and vertical integration, unlocking 300 bps from mRNA expansions.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Alex Patel with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Alex Patel, Morgan Stanley:
On clinical, updates for ATH-301 PFS readout risks?

Dr. Emily Chen, Chief Medical Officer:
Alex, futility cleared, 68% Phase 2 ORR de-risks. 90% power, RMAT/PRIME accelerate. Enrollment diverse globally, companion diagnostic 92% sensitive.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Sophia Grant with Bank of America. Please go ahead.

Sophia Grant, Bank of America:
Thanks. Patent cliff mitigation for Nexavolt—NASH impact?

Michael Rivera, CFO:
Sophia, NASH 45% fat reduction adds $1.2 billion TAM, XR oral $900 million. 65% revenues preserved via expansions, M&A, projecting 8-10% CAGR post-trough.

Operator:
Thank you. There are no further questions at this time.

Johnathan Hale, CEO:
Thank you for your questions. In closing, I want to thank our employees for their hard work and dedication. We are confident in our ability to continue to execute on our strategic priorities and deliver long-term value for our shareholders.

Sarah Jenkins, Head of Investor Relations:
Thank you for joining us today. This concludes the NovaBiotech Therapeutics Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. Have a great day.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
